extraction_metadata.scope_note: This article is a systematic review, not a primary clinical study. ATOM captures the review's own methods, synthesis, limitations, conclusions, and selected secondary-reported quantitative results. Secondary-reported results are tagged and must not be treated as if this review enrolled the underlying patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review aimed to scrutinize the available literature, present published data and documentation, and analyze risks associated with cervical and lumbar epidural corticosteroid injections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This systematic review aims to scrutinise the available literature

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that the review followed PRISMA guidance and used a standardized protocol with prespecified objectives and inclusion criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This review was carried out in accordance to the PRISMA guidelines

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible studies were English-language original articles published from September 1994 through September 2014 that reported complications related to cervical or lumbar ESI and specified the injection approach.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Publications from the last 20 years (September 1994 to September 2014)

population.label: English-language original studies of cervical or lumbar epidural corticosteroid injections

atoms.canonical_statement: The search covered PubMed MEDLINE, Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PubMed MEDLINE, Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Library

atoms.canonical_statement: Search terms included epidural, injection, corticosteroid, steroid, transforaminal, interlaminar, adverse events, complication, and side effect, and bibliographies were manually searched for additional studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The terms used for the search included

atoms.canonical_statement: Two authors assessed citations independently, without blinding, using a standardized process; full manuscripts were reviewed when title or abstract was insufficient.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: in an independent, unblinded and standardised manner
